sections.text_helper: Section 49.2.3 "DBG reset and clocks" in chapter 49 (Debug support (DBG)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 2415.
sections.section_content:
The debug port (SWJ-DP) is reset by a power-on reset and when waking up from Standby
mode.
The debugger supplies the clock for the debug port via the debug interface pin
JTCK/SWCLK. This clock is used to register the serial input data in both serial-wire and
JTAG modes, as well as to operate the state machines and internal logic of the debug port.
This clock must therefore continue to toggle for several cycles after the end of an access,
toensure that the debug port returns to the idle state.
The SWJ-DP contains an asynchronous interface to the DCLK domain that covers the rest
of the SWJ-DP and the access port.
The DCLK is a gated version of the system clock.
The DCLK domain is enabled by the debugger using CDBGPWRUPREQ. The DCLK is
disabled at power-up, and must be disabled when the debugger is disconnected, to avoid
wasting energy.
The debug and trace components included in the processor are clocked with the processor
clock.
Caution: To avoid a lockup situation when accessing the TPIU registers (except ID registers), it is
necessary to activate the TRCENA bit (bit 24, trace enable) of the DEMCR register
(0xE000EDFC) of the Cortex M33.
